title: The Occupational Pension Schemes (Investment) Regulations 2005, regulation 4 (Investment by trustees)
note: Latest available revised text. Reg 4(2): scheme assets must be invested in the best interests of members and beneficiaries and, where there is a potential conflict of interest, in their sole interest. Reg 4(3): security, quality, liquidity and profitability of the portfolio as a whole. Reg 7 disapplies reg 4 for schemes with fewer than 100 members (seen in search result, not fetched).

title: Pensions Act 1995, section 36 (Choosing investments)
note: s.36(3): before investing, trustees must obtain and consider proper advice on whether the investment is satisfactory. s.36(4): trustees must decide at what intervals to take such advice on retained investments, and take it.

title: Pensions Act 1995, section 34 (Power of investment and delegation)
note: s.34(2): investment discretion may be delegated to a fund manager. s.34(4): trustees are not responsible for the fund manager's act or default if they have taken all reasonable steps to satisfy themselves that the manager has appropriate knowledge and experience and is carrying out the work competently.

title: Tender for fiduciary management services (detailed guidance for trustees)
note: Page shows 'Last updated: August 2022'. Trustees must carry out a qualifying tender process when selecting fiduciary management providers for 20% or more of scheme assets; a qualifying tender means bids from at least three unconnected providers; duties sit in regulations in force from 1 October 2022; trustees should review the provider's performance and periodically review the market. Only the first 100,000 characters of the page were read.

title: Serving UK pension schemes better: final decision from the CMA's investigation into investment consultancy (final report overview)
note: Findings describe the UK market as investigated up to 2018, not today. Low engagement by some trustees; firms offering both consultancy and fiduciary management have an incumbency advantage; half of schemes bought fiduciary management from their existing consultant; relatively high switching costs; remedies include mandatory tendering and fee and performance disclosure.

title: FG22/5 Final non-Handbook Guidance for firms on the Consumer Duty
note: Paras 2.10, 2.12, 2.13, 2.29 and the investments scope bullet read from the PDF. For investments the Duty applies to business with a customer who is not a professional client; it applies across the distribution chain to firms that determine or materially influence retail customer outcomes, even without a direct relationship. Para 4.2 quotes Principle 7 (communicate information in a way which is clear, fair and not misleading) and para 2.11 says Principles 6 and 7 continue to apply to customers outside the Duty. The in-force dates (31 July 2023 open products, 31 July 2024 closed products) were seen in a search summary only.

title: FCA Handbook, COBS 2.1.1R (the client's best interests rule)
note: The Handbook page would not render for automated reading. Rule wording ('honestly, fairly and professionally in accordance with the best interests of its client') is taken from search-result text and from cross-references in COBS 2.3. Check the exact current wording and its application to professional clients on the Handbook before quoting.

title: Record number of buy-ins in 2025 with the busiest H2 ever as competition intensifies (press release)
note: Figures describe calendar 2025: 367 buy-ins totalling £38.2bn (2023: £49.1bn; 2024: £47.8bn; 2024: 298 transactions). LCP is a consultancy active in this market; its count differs slightly from other consultancies' counts.

title: An Integrative Model of Organizational Trust (Mayer, Davis and Schoorman), Academy of Management Review 20(3), 709-734
note: Academic framework that separates ability, benevolence and integrity as bases of trustworthiness. Cited from general knowledge of the paper, not re-read for this project. Used only as a way of organising the discussion.
